title: Integrate perf-canary gates into Runtime LTS patch release process
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
We need perf-canary results to be a first-class gate for Runtime LTS patch releases (e.g., 1.18.1-lts, 1.18.2-lts). This ticket covers:

1) Defining the required benchmark sets for each LTS patch.
2) Defining regression thresholds (latency + throughput) and the waiver/override process.
3) Wiring perf-canary summary artifacts into the release-branch CI so Release Eng can block/promote RC builds with an auditable signal.

Why:
- LTS customers (Dedicated + Private) are extremely sensitive to performance drift. A “correctness-only” gate is insufficient; we need repeatable, comparable perf signals across canonical workloads and GPU SKUs before publishing artifacts.
- We’ve already seen regressions on minor runtime upgrades (e.g., p95 latency shifts under mixed prompt lengths) and benchmark noise; we need clear policy for reruns vs waivers.

Out of scope:
- Rewriting perf-canary infrastructure; we’ll use existing harness and extend workflows/outputs.
- Adding new benchmarks unrelated to LTS stability (feature benchmarking can continue on mainline).
acceptance_criteria:
- Release branches (runtime-*-lts) trigger perf-canary benchmark workflows and publish a machine-readable summary artifact + human-readable report link.
- LTS patch RC promotion is blocked unless perf gate passes (or a waiver is explicitly approved and recorded).
- Required benchmark suite is documented and includes at minimum: mixed prompt length chat, long context chat, overload/backpressure scenario, and batch/throughput sweep.
- Regression thresholds are defined for p50/p95 latency and throughput, including handling of noisy runs (rerun policy).
- Gate results are surfaced in release PR checklist / release manager view with a single pass/fail plus drill-down.
- Waiver process is documented (who can approve, how it’s recorded, and when waivers are allowed).
benchmarks_required_for_each_lts_patch:
Required benchmark sets (must run on each LTS patch RC):

A) Chat – mixed lengths (Scheduling sensitivity)
- Dataset: “chat-mix-short-long” (mixture of ~0.5–2k input tokens, ~128–512 output tokens)
- Purpose: catch regressions in scheduling fairness, batching heuristics, and tail latency.

B) Chat – long context (Kernel/KV cache sensitivity)
- Dataset: “chat-long-context” (~8k–16k input tokens, ~128 output tokens)
- Purpose: catch KV cache growth/compaction and attention kernel regressions that hit memory bandwidth.

C) Overload/backpressure scenario (Stability under load)
- Dataset: “burst-overload-2x” (bursty arrival, target utilization > 90%)
- Purpose: catch scheduler starvation/backpressure regressions; tail latency blowups; queueing behavior changes.

D) Throughput sweep (Economics)
- Dataset: “throughput-sweep” (controlled concurrency ramp)
- Purpose: validate tokens/sec stability and continuous batching behavior.

GPU coverage (minimum for LTS gate):
- H100 80GB (primary)
- A100 80GB (enterprise baseline)

Optional/Best-effort (non-blocking but reported):
- L40S (cost-optimized Dedicated tiers)
- Multi-node sharded (if patch touches sharding/collectives) — separate ticket if needed.
thresholds_and_gate_policy:
Gate metrics (computed vs pinned baseline for the LTS branch):

Blocking thresholds (default):
- p95 end-to-end latency regression: > +3% on any required benchmark = FAIL
- p50 end-to-end latency regression: > +5% on any required benchmark = FAIL
- Throughput regression (tokens/sec): < -2% on any required benchmark = FAIL
- Error rate: any increase above 0.1% absolute on benchmark runs = FAIL

Non-blocking reported thresholds (warn-only, requires note in release notes if exceeded):
- p95 latency regression between +2% and +3% = WARN
- Throughput regression between -1% and -2% = WARN

Noise handling / rerun policy:
- Each benchmark runs 3 iterations; gate uses median-of-3.
- If variance across the 3 runs exceeds 2.5% for p95 or throughput, mark as “NOISY” and require 1 full rerun (another 3 iterations) on a fresh runner.
- If still noisy, Release Manager may proceed only with an explicit waiver and an incident-style note in the release thread (include runner IDs and variance stats).

Waivers:
- Allowed only for known benchmark infra issues or explicitly accepted trade-offs (e.g., correctness fix with small perf cost).
- Must be approved by: Marcus Reed (Perf suite owner) + Connor O’Brien (Release Eng) + Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes (SRE).
- Waiver must be linked in the release PR and summarized in LTS release notes under “Performance notes” (even if customer-facing language is softened).
implementation_notes:
Integration approach:
- perf-canary repo owns the benchmark workflows and produces:
  1) JSON summary (pass/fail + deltas per metric)
  2) Markdown report (graphs + tables + run metadata)
- runtime repo release CI (release/* or runtime-*-lts) will:
  - trigger perf-canary workflow via dispatch (branch + commit SHA + baseline tag)
  - wait for completion
  - fetch summary artifact
  - fail the job if summary=FAIL (unless waiver label present + approvals recorded)

Baseline semantics:
- Baseline is pinned per LTS line (e.g., runtime-1.18-lts baseline tag) and only updated when we intentionally accept perf movement.
- Baseline update requires the same approvals as a waiver, plus a note in the LTS known-issues/perf section (so drift is auditable).

Surfacing:
- Status checks on the release PR: “perf-gate (H100)”, “perf-gate (A100)”.
- A single consolidated summary link posted to the release coordination thread + attached to the release notes PR.

Open question resolved in-thread (see comments): whether to gate on p99. Decision: do NOT gate on p99 for now due to measurement instability; report p99 as informational and revisit after 2 patches of data.
comments: 2025-02-07 (Connor O’Brien): Creating this as a P0 for LTS. Without a perf gate we’re going to keep shipping “stable” patches that move tail latency. Marcus can you propose the minimum benchmark set + thresholds that are defensible for enterprise? Please align with SRE on waiver process (we need something auditable).

2025-02-10 (Marcus Reed): Drafting benchmark sets A–D based on the failures we’ve actually seen: (1) mixed prompt length tail changes, (2) long-context KV/cache issues, (3) overload/backpressure behavior, (4) throughput economics. Re: metrics, I recommend p50 + p95 + tokens/sec; p99 is too noisy right now on shared runners.

2025-02-11 (Allison Grant): +1 to gating p95. Please also include error rate/timeout counts as a hard fail. We’ve had “perf improvements” that were actually partial failures/retries in the harness. Also request that we store runner metadata (GPU UUID, driver, clocks) in the report for auditability.

2025-02-12 (Jonas Weber): Thresholds: p95 +3% seems reasonable given we’ll use median-of-3 and fixed configs. Suggest adding a variance check and mandatory rerun before calling something a regression. Otherwise release week gets blocked by flake and we’ll end up waiving everything.

2025-02-13 (Claire Dubois): On long-context: please lock the prompt set and decoding params for LTS (temperature=0, top_p=1, fixed max_new_tokens). Otherwise comparisons are meaningless between patches. Also strongly prefer a warm-up phase that’s excluded from metrics.

2025-02-18 (Sahana Iyer): From CI perspective: we can gate release branches via a dispatch into perf-canary and then read back an artifact. We should avoid cross-repo secrets with broad scopes; propose a dedicated GitHub App token limited to workflow dispatch + artifact read.

2025-02-25 (Marcus Reed): Implemented median-of-3 + variance detection. If variance >2.5%, mark run as NOISY and require rerun. Also added explicit baseline tag support per LTS line so we don’t accidentally compare to mainline.

2025-03-03 (Sean Gallagher): Waiver policy looks good. Please make sure waivers are rare and recorded. Requirement from SRE: if we waive due to perf infra noise, we must schedule a follow-up run within 48h on dedicated runners and post results to the release thread.

2025-03-10 (Connor O’Brien): We’ll treat perf gate as hard block for publish. If we need to ship for security reasons, we can use the emergency procedure + waiver (still requires SRE approval). Updating runbook accordingly in ENG-4830/Confluence.

2025-03-18 (Marcus Reed): Marking Done. perf-canary workflows for LTS branches merged, thresholds tightened, and release CI now consumes the perf summary artifact. Ran against runtime-1.18-lts RC and got clean pass on H100/A100. Remaining TODO (non-blocking): add L40S warn-only runs once runner capacity is provisioned (tracked under INT-3368).
